sources.name: IRCC Study Permit — Eligibility
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Confirm valid letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI), PAL/TAL or Quebec CAQ requirement/exemption, sufficient funds for tuition + living expenses + return transportation, admissibility/medical or police documents if requested, and that the applicant will leave Canada when authorised stay ends. Eligibility is case-specific; an LOA or PAL/TAL does not guarantee approval. Check the applicant's nationality-specific IRCC visa-office instructions. Detection is not legal interpretation.
sources.verification_mode: Availability-only automated check; manual legal review required

sources.name: Department of Home Affairs — Student visa subclass 500
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify exact CRICOS provider/course/campus and valid CoE for every intended course; CoE must remain valid at lodgement and decision. Check Genuine Student criterion and 150-word online responses, academic history, course rationale, home-country ties/economic circumstances, employment and immigration history. Run the personalised Home Affairs Document Checklist Tool using passport country and principal provider; attach financial/English evidence if listed. Published 12-month living costs: AUD 29,710 student, AUD 10,394 partner, AUD 4,449 child; add first 12 months tuition, travel, and applicable schooling costs (published guide AUD 13,502 per school-age child/year); check pro-rata method and current amounts before lodgement. Evidence must show genuine access and source of funds; one-day balance alone may be insufficient. Maintain OSHC for all applicants unless exempt. English scores/exemptions depend on current test-date rules and individual checklist. Most students may work 48 hours/fortnight while course in session; research master's/doctoral students and family may have no cap after course begins; verify VEVO/grant conditions. Since 2 Oct 2026, most applications must be lodged offshore unless applicant meets an eligible onshore category; family inclusion rules changed and need individual review. Do not guarantee work, approval, processing time or post-study outcomes. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Fee Paying Student Visa
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify current approved provider and NZQA Code signatory status, exact course/campus/NZQCF level and offer of place. Tuition evidence generally required for 1 year or programme (shorter); tuition is additional to maintenance. Tertiary/English/non-compulsory study funds: NZD 20,000/year or NZD 1,667/month for shorter study; school students NZD 17,000/year or NZD 1,417/month. Also prove outward travel. Primary evidence may include 3 months of bank transactions, term deposit held 3 months, scholarship or qualifying education loan; explain deposits over NZD 2,000 and source of funds. Sri Lankan nationals may be eligible for Funds Transfer Scheme if INZ directs. Check health, character, insurance and individual checklist. Genuine intentions include course rationale, prior study, funding, immigration history and future plans. From 27 Oct 2026 eligible student work up to 25 hours/week; new master's-by-research applications on/after that date no longer have unlimited work. Relevant student visa expiry is generally 2 months after course end instead of 1 month; 31 March expiry remains unchanged. Check eVisa. PSWV depends on exact NZQCF level and study length; degree level 7+ usually 30 weeks full-time in NZ; eligible non-degree L4-7 only on INZ list and work related to study; PSWV requires at least NZD 5,000 and deadlines usually 3 months (doctoral 6 months; specific cases 12). Verify current announcements and application dates; no guaranteed job, visa or residence.

sources.name: U.S. Department of State — Student Visa (F/M categories, SEVIS and Form I-20)
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify correct F-1 or M-1 category, SEVP-certified school/programme, SEVIS registration and signed Form I-20, DS-160, academic preparation, credible funds based on the school's I-20 estimate, intent to depart after authorised study, and current Colombo post instructions. Current published fees: USD 185 nonimmigrant visa application fee (DOS) plus separate USD 350 I-901 SEVIS fee for F/M students; recheck official fee pages before payment and match the I-901 receipt to the current I-20 SEVIS ID. New F/M visas may be issued up to 365 days before course start, but new students may not enter more than 30 days before start. Visa issuance does not guarantee admission at the port of entry. Sri Lankan residents should follow current post-location guidance for their country of nationality or residence. No universal government bank-balance amount. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Issuing a residency permit to a student
sources.note: Primary Dubai operational source. The educational institution is the student's host/guarantor for this non-working student residence route. GDRFA published core documents: recent colour photo with white background, passport copy, approved medical examination, Emirates ID application receipt and health insurance. Institution must be licensed and have Ministry of Education or relevant emirate education-authority approval. Published service page currently lists AED 200 residence permit fee plus AED 10 Knowledge Dirham, AED 10 Innovation Dirham, AED 500 inside-country fee (if applicable), AED 20 delivery; fees may change and are not an all-in student budget. Expected completion is listed as 48 hours, not a guarantee. Page states 60 days after expiry/cancellation. Confirm sponsor, fees, documents, timing and grace-period category directly with GDRFA/institution for each case. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: European Commission — Who does what in EU immigration
Federal ICP — Renewal of residence permits (includes student and sponsor/host grace-period categories)
sources.note: Official ICP renewal service page. It lists a 180-day grace period for students after completing their studies and a 60-day grace period for residence permits issued with a guarantor or host. The page displays a last-updated date of 11 December 2024. GDRFA Dubai's student-residence service page separately states 60 days after expiry/cancellation, while ICP's student-specific issuance page states 180 days after study completion. This is an apparent official-source discrepancy: do not quote a grace period to a client until GDRFA/ICP confirms the exact permit category, emirate and circumstances in writing. Detection is not legal interpretation.
